turns.context:
Clean the Goodreads sources into a single persistent working set for all later tasks. Use books.id as the analysis book_key.
ratings.book_id and to_read.book_id join to books.id; book_tags.goodreads_book_id joins to books.book_id. Before computing rating activity, if a (user_id, book_id) pair appears more than once in ratings, remove all rating rows for that repeated pair rather than keeping one row. Remove all books sharing an exact raw books.original_title value; do not use normalized title keys for this duplicate-title removal. The cleaned table excludes records missing original_title, authors, average_rating, ratings_count, or star-rating columns. After component percentile ranks are built on the cleaned table, the active review range excludes books without known language, known publication year, or a recognized main genre.
Use two title treatments based on original_title. The early key lowercases and collapses spaces without folding accents, while the stricter key later removes parenthetical text, removes standalone articles, replaces non-alphanumeric characters with spaces, lowercases,
and collapses spaces.
Connect reading-intent counts and genre evidence to the correct book records. Recognize genre evidence only from exact normalized tag names in these families: art, biography, business, chick-lit, children and childrens, christian, classics, comics, contemporary, cookbooks, crime, ebooks, fantasy, fiction, historical-fiction, history, horror, humor, manga, memoir, music, mystery, nonfiction, paranormal, philosophy, poetry, romance, science, science-fiction, self-help, sports, suspense, thriller, travel, and young-adult. Normalize tag names by lowercasing and replacing underscores with hyphens. Map recognized tags to canonical genre families, including children and childrens -> children, historical-fiction -> historical_fiction, science-fiction -> science_fiction, self-help -> self_help, young-adult -> young_adult, and chick-lit -> chick_lit. For each book_key, sum tag counts within each canonical genre, choose the main genre by largest summed count, and break ties alphabetically by canonical genre.
Keep analysis-ready fields for title matching, lead author, language, star-rating diagnostics, reading intent, and genre rarity. Build component percentile ranks on the cleaned table before applying the active review filter; percentile ranks use average tie handling and pandas style rank(pct=True) * 100, i.e. average_rank / nonmissing_count * 100. Do not rescale ranks with (rank - 1) / (n - 1).
In the early genre-scarcity treatment, rarer recognized main genres receive higher scores. The active review range excludes books without known language, known publication year, or a recognized main genre.
The first review score blends 34% reader-intent volume, 24% exposure gap where lower Goodreads rating count is stronger, 22% genre rarity, and 20% average-rating quality. Define demand_absolute_score as the percentile rank of reading-intent count. Keep active-range books whose demand_absolute_score alone reaches the active-range 80th percentile; do not include exposure gap in this filtering threshold. Also require raw Goodreads rating count to be no higher than the active-range 85th percentile. Sort ranked outputs by the named score in the natural direction implied by the question; tied ranked rows and top-N truncation use the smaller book_key first.
Restore display titles, full authors, covers, publication years, raw star columns, ISBN fields, and raw tag rows only when an audit needs source evidence. Throughout this analysis, compute derived quantities including sums, gaps, ratios, means, similarities, and correlations using unrounded values, and report decimal-valued final results rounded to 3 decimal places. Counts use the cleaned denominator established in the same step unless the question explicitly asks for a comparison across two states. Absent neighbor evidence contributes zero.
This step establishes the persistent cleaned analysis state for all later tasks; later tasks must reuse these book keys, cleaned ratings, genre assignments, title keys, and percentile columns unless explicitly instructed to recompute one component.
turns.question: Build the first review pool by combining reader intent, exposure gap, genre scarcity, and quality. Show the five leading books and the component contributions behind their scores.
turns.solution: First review pool: 750 books from 8,160 active-range books. Active thresholds were demand_absolute_score >= 81.669 and ratings_count <= 72,676.200. Top five by first_review_score: 1. book_key 7884, Stephen King's N. by Marc Guggenheim, Alex Maleev, Stephen King, genre horror, intent 154, ratings_count 10,844, avg_rating 4.220, score 83.161; component scores demand/exposure/scarcity/quality = 85.144/88.340/76.008/81.445; weighted contributions = 28.949/21.202/16.722/16.289. 2. book_key 7297, All But My Life: A Memoir by Gerda Weissmann Klein, genre memoir, intent 127, ratings_count 13,710, avg_rating 4.280, score 81.941; component scores = 81.669/74.932/84.330/88.187; weighted contributions = 27.767/17.984/18.553/17.637. 3. book_key 7275, Far from the Tree: Parents, Children, and the Search for Identity by Andrew Solomon, genre nonfiction, intent 137, ratings_count 11,879, avg_rating 4.260, score 81.545; component scores = 82.958/83.193/73.314/86.220; weighted contributions = 28.206/19.966/16.129/17.244. 4. book_key 8362, Evicted: Poverty and Profit in the American City by Matthew Desmond, genre nonfiction, intent 131, ratings_count 15,165, avg_rating 4.480, score 80.336; component scores = 82.248/68.987/73.314/98.426; weighted contributions = 27.964/16.557/16.129/19.685. 5. book_key 6810, America's First Daughter by Stephanie Dray, Laura Kamoie, genre historical_fiction, intent 200, ratings_count 13,279, avg_rating 4.220, score 79.649; component scores = 89.192/76.904/66.261/81.445; weighted contributions = 30.325/18.457/14.577/16.289.
turns.reasoning_summary: Used only the allowed Goodbooks CSVs. I removed missing required book records and all exact raw original_title duplicates, removed every rating row belonging to repeated (user_id, book_id) pairs, joined intent counts on books.id and genre evidence on books.book_id, assigned canonical main genres by summed tag counts with alphabetical tie-breaks, built pandas-style percentile components on the cleaned table, then applied the active-range demand and ratings_count filters and sorted by score descending with book_key ascending for ties.

turns.context: Keep the cleaned book range and first-pass scoring setup, but measure demand by the percentile rank of reading-intent count divided by cleaned rating activity. Books with no cleaned rating activity have an intent rate of zero. The early high-intent group is the first 25 rows from the initial review pool.
turns.question: Rebuild the review pool with relative demand. Show five leading books, the books entering and leaving the ten-book monitoring set, and whether the movement mainly comes from books already in the early high-intent group.
turns.solution:
Relative-demand review pool: 742 books from 8,160 active-range books. Filters used relative_demand_score >= 81.681 and ratings_count <= 72,676.200.

Five leading books by relative_review_score:
1. book_key 7884, Stephen King's N., score 83.113; intent/rating activity 154/100 = 1.540; component scores demand/exposure/scarcity/quality = 85.002/88.340/76.008/81.445; contributions = 28.901/21.202/16.722/16.289.
2. book_key 7297, All But My Life: A Memoir, score 82.199; intent/rating activity 127/95 = 1.337; component scores = 82.428/74.932/84.330/88.187; contributions = 28.026/17.984/18.553/17.637.
3. book_key 7275, Far from the Tree: Parents, Children, and the Search for Identity, score 81.499; intent/rating activity 137/100 = 1.370; component scores = 82.822/83.193/73.314/86.220; contributions = 28.159/19.966/16.129/17.244.
4. book_key 8362, Evicted: Poverty and Profit in the American City, score 80.501; intent/rating activity 131/96 = 1.365; component scores = 82.734/68.987/73.314/98.426; contributions = 28.130/16.557/16.129/19.685.
5. book_key 6810, America's First Daughter, score 79.632; intent/rating activity 200/100 = 2.000; component scores = 89.143/76.904/66.261/81.445; contributions = 30.309/18.457/14.577/16.289.

Ten-book monitoring set movement: entered book_key 1851, The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer, initial pool rank 11 -> relative rank 9, relative score 77.054, relative demand 96.520, in early high-intent group: true. Left book_key 6793, Glory over Everything: Beyond The Kitchen House, initial rank 7 -> outside rebuilt pool, relative score 77.343, relative demand 81.532, in early high-intent group: true.

Movement assessment: yes, the movement mainly comes from books already in the early high-intent group. The only entrant and the only leaver were both in the first 25 rows of the initial review pool, so this is an intra-early-group reshuffle rather than outside titles entering the monitoring set.
turns.reasoning_summary: Reused the turn-1 cleaned books, cleaned ratings, genre assignments, and percentile components. Computed intent_per_cleaned_rating as reading_intent_count divided by cleaned_rating_activity_count, using zero for books with no cleaned activity, ranked that rate with pandas-style percentile ranks on the cleaned table, rebuilt the weighted score with the same 34/24/22/20 formula and the same active-range/rating-cap setup, then compared initial and rebuilt top-ten sets.

turns.context: Shrink lightly exposed titles toward the overall rating level. Use the 60th percentile of Goodreads rating count as the exposure floor, compute the overall mean weighted by Goodreads rating count, weight each book's own average by its Goodreads rating count relative to that count plus the exposure floor, weight the overall mean by the remaining floor share, and percentile-rank the blended value. Use the earlier volume-based demand lens here. Flip strength is the absolute value of the unweighted sum of the demand-percentile gap and quality-percentile gap between the compared treatments.
turns.question: Find books whose membership in the ten-book monitoring set changes when volume demand is paired with exposure-aware quality. Show up to five strongest flips and the score components behind each movement.
turns.solution:
Exposure-aware quality used ratings_count floor 26,970.000 and overall weighted mean rating 4.038. The rebuilt pool kept the volume-demand filter, with 750 books; top-ten keys changed from [7884, 7297, 7275, 8362, 6810, 2958, 6793, 3953, 9993, 6425] to [7884, 7297, 7275, 8362, 2958, 6810, 1851, 9993, 3953, 5640].

Entered: 1851, 5640. Left: 6793, 6425. Flip strength uses |demand percentile gap + quality percentile gap|; demand gap is 0.000 for all because this treatment keeps volume demand.

Strongest membership flips:
1. Left: book_key 6793, Glory over Everything: Beyond The Kitchen House. Rank 7 -> 12, score 77.389 -> 76.075, flip_strength 6.573. Demand pct 81.669, quality pct 83.876 -> 77.303. Contributions demand/exposure/scarcity/quality were 27.767/18.269/14.577/16.775, with quality changing to 15.461.
2. Left: book_key 6425, Here be Dragons (Welsh Princes, #1). Rank 10 -> 13, score 77.087 -> 76.048, flip_strength 5.196. Demand pct 84.597, quality pct 90.192 -> 84.996. Contributions were 28.763/15.708/14.577/18.038, with quality changing to 16.999.
3. Entered: book_key 1851, The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer. Rank 11 -> 7, score 77.062 -> 77.999, flip_strength 4.688. Demand pct 96.541, quality pct 89.247 -> 93.935. Contributions were 32.824/5.243/21.145/17.849, with quality changing to 18.787.
4. Entered: book_key 5640, Rising Strong. Rank 13 -> 10, score 76.327 -> 76.377, flip_strength 0.251. Demand pct 85.144, quality pct 77.423 -> 77.675. Contributions were 28.949/11.789/20.104/15.485, with quality changing to 15.535.
turns.reasoning_summary: Reused the persisted turn-1 cleaned books and initial review pool. Computed exposure-aware quality on the cleaned table using the 60th percentile of ratings_count as the shrinkage floor and the ratings_count-weighted mean average_rating as the prior, percentile-ranked the blended quality, rebuilt the original volume-demand score with the new quality component, and compared the original and exposure-aware top-ten monitoring sets. Flip strength was computed from unweighted percentile gaps; demand gap is zero because the demand lens did not change.

Classify source risk by duplicate cleaned title, then more than two listed authors, then fewer than three restored recognized genre-tag rows; otherwise mark the risk as low_source_risk.

turns.context: Some titles become unstable under stricter title alignment because series suffixes, leading articles, and punctuation can collapse separate display names. Move title alignment to the stricter treatment while keeping the current demand, quality, and scarcity treatments. This changes matching keys, feature text, and collision risk, without merging or deleting book records. Focus on candidates that appeared in at least two of the three ten-book monitoring sets. Title-risk score adds 25 points when the stricter title key has more collisions than the earlier key, 20 points when original-title length is no greater than the cleaned-table median, and 10 points when the restored author string lists more than two authors.
turns.question: Re-audit the stable candidates after stricter title alignment. Show five candidates most affected by title merging, short-title status, or author ambiguity, and summarize how the stable candidate set changes.
turns.solution:
Stable candidate set: the three monitoring sets had 12 unique book_keys; requiring appearance in at least two sets leaves 10 stable candidates: [1851, 2958, 3953, 6425, 6810, 7275, 7297, 7884, 8362, 9993]. Eight appeared in all three sets and two appeared in exactly two. Stricter title alignment changed key text for 8 of 10, but did not create extra strict-title collisions for any stable candidate, so no book records are merged or removed.

Median cleaned-table original_title length: 18.000. Five highest title-risk candidates:
1. book_key 7884, Stephen King's N.; strict_title_key: stephen king s n; appearances: 3; early/strict collision counts: 0/0; title length 17, short: true; authors: Marc Guggenheim, Alex Maleev, Stephen King; author_count 3; title_risk_score 30.
2. book_key 6425, Here be Dragons; strict_title_key: here be dragons; appearances: 2; early/strict collision counts: 0/0; title length 15, short: true; authors: Sharon Kay Penman; author_count 1; title_risk_score 20.
3. book_key 7297, All But My Life; strict_title_key: all but my life; appearances: 3; early/strict collision counts: 0/0; title length 15, short: true; authors: Gerda Weissmann Klein; author_count 1; title_risk_score 20.
4. book_key 1851, The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer; strict_title_key: emperor of all maladies biography of cancer; appearances: 2; early/strict collision counts: 0/0; title length 50, short: false; authors: Siddhartha Mukherjee; author_count 1; title_risk_score 0.
5. book_key 2958, Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid; strict_title_key: gödel escher bach eternal golden braid; appearances: 3; early/strict collision counts: 0/0; title length 44, short: false; authors: Douglas R. Hofstadter; author_count 1; title_risk_score 0.

Risk summary: title-merging risk affected 0 stable candidates, short-title risk affected 3, author-ambiguity risk affected 1, and 3 candidates had nonzero title-risk scores. The stable book-key set itself is unchanged under stricter alignment; only the matching keys and risk annotations change.
turns.reasoning_summary: Loaded the three persisted top-ten monitoring sets, counted book appearances, retained candidates appearing in at least two sets, and computed strict-vs-early title collision counts across the full cleaned table. Title-risk score used +25 for increased strict-key collisions, +20 for original_title length <= cleaned-table median, and +10 for more than two listed authors. Ranked stable candidates by title_risk_score descending with book_key ascending for ties.
